rewrites.summary:
Same-sex conduct is legal in Gibraltar with an equal age of consent since 2012, discrimination protections covering sexual orientation and gender reassignment have stood since 2007, and same-sex marriage—enacted unanimously in December 2016 after civil partnerships from 2014 and a 2015 public consultation that returned overwhelming support—gives a trans visitor's marriage full recognition.

The standing gap affects documents: no route exists to change legal gender, so local law offers no mechanism for recognising a gender-marker change. Practical safety is the other gap: there was no specific hate-crime provision denigrating a person for sexual orientation until July 2021, when the Ministry for Justice said it would 'urgently' consider one after a wave of online homophobia during Pride month drew a rare public rebuke from the head of government.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Parent-state policy turbulence: governance is subject to regular parliamentary scrutiny by the United Kingdom's overseas-territories committee, which has pressed accountability standards across the portfolio.

Adjacent political context to the marriage law: a news report described the December 2015 consultation as leaving locals polarized, with a government minister presiding over an inter-ministerial committee weighing all viewpoints while the main parties suggested support.
rewrites.localsOnly:
The 2015 consultation drew 3,490 replies from a 24,117-person electorate — a resident-input detail of the law's passage.

An adoption right was established in 2013 by the highest court's ruling, governing resident family formation.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes:
Jurisdiction note carried on the record: a territory of the United Kingdom, with local deviations from the parent state's framework flagged in the summary. Whether the hate-crime provision the Ministry for Justice said in July 2021 it would 'urgently' consider has since been enacted is unresolved in this record; no enforcement data for the 2007 discrimination protections appears in the sources.

One 2016 news report framed the December 2015 consultation as leaving locals polarized where the record summary records overwhelming support. Core facts were confirmed by the record's freshness check against a reference retrieved on 2026-09-28.
